messages:
Priya Nair: Quick heads-up — we need a rolling soft-reboot across az21 to apply a vendor switch-fabric microcode fix. Affects top-of-rack switches in three racks. Planning window: Tue 2025-06-10 02:00-06:00 UTC.
Alex Soto: How big is the expected capacity hit? GPUs or networking only?
Priya Nair: Networking primarily. We'll cordon nodes behind the impacted racks for ~10-15m each; some pods will reschedule. Expected net GPU-serving capacity drop ~10-14% during peak of ops while backfill grabs spare nodes.
Jared Kim: Can we do cohorted drains? i.e., 2 racks at a time with 30m gap?
Priya Nair: Yes — cohort plan: 2 racks -> 15m drain + verification -> 30m cool -> next 2. Total ~4 cohorts. Canary first on rack-az21-c1 (low-traffic).
Marta Lopez: We should notify any high-commitment Dedicated customers in az21. I'll craft a short comms blurb. @Priya Nair, need an ETA for when we'll re-route traffic to other regions if failure.
Priya Nair: If telemetry shows p95 latency > 150ms or error increase > 1.5x during canary, we abort and rollback microcode. Fail-safe: canary at 02:00 UTC; if good, continue with cohorts starting 02:45.
Alex Soto: How are we handling KV cache and prefix caches? Will those warmups require extra time?
Priya Nair: We'll seed KV cache on standby nodes before draining using our cache-warm job. Command for seed (run from ops jumpbox):
```
./cache-seed --region=az21 --pools=standby --seed-set=last-24h-prompts
kubectl label node rack-az21-c1 canary=true
```
Priya Nair: Also enabling automatic fallback routing to eu-west1 if cohort health drops below 90% for >3m.
Jared Kim: Backfill plan? Spot vs reserved? Cost delta?
Priya Nair: Primary backfill from reserved warm pool; we will dip into spot if reserved saturation > 80%. Estimated incremental cost for the 4h window ~ $1,200 (worst-case if we use mix of spot -> reserved node spinups).
Marta Lopez: Draft comms: "Scheduled network maintenance in az21 may cause transient request latency and short task reschedules between 02:00-06:00 UTC on 2025-06-10. We'll stagger changes and monitor closely; rollback plan in place." Thoughts?
Alex Soto: Add a note about canary and abort thresholds + contact SRE oncall.
Priya Nair: Good call. Ops checklist (short):
- create calendar event + maintenance tag
- run cache-seed on standby nodes
- label canary node and run validation harness
- cohort drain: cordon -> drain (kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data) -> verify telemetry -> uncordon if rollback
- escalate to oncall if p95>150ms or errors>1.5x

Jared Kim: I'll be oncall during the window and will watch scheduler/evac logs. please ping me in thread when canary starts.
ops-bot: Maintenance event created: az21-switch-fabric-soft-reboot on 2025-06-10 02:00-06:00 UTC; calendar invite sent to #eng-infra and oncall.
Marta Lopez: I'll post the customer advisory by EOD, cc legal for the wording.
Priya Nair: Thanks everyone — will post the final runbook and exact rack sequence before EOD. Ping here for any changes.
Alex Soto: 👍 keep the rollback steps handy (microcode revert and switch warm reboot)
Priya Nair: Copy that. Last note: avoid doing this during peak ML eval batch windows — blocked window already set from 01:30-06:30 to keep teams aware.
